article_title: A Study of Geometry Content Knowledge of Elementary Preservice Teachers
citation: Fatma Aslan-Tutak and Thomasenia Lott Adams. (2015). A Study of Geometry Content Knowledge of Elementary Preservice Teachers. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 7(3), 301-318. https://www.iejee.com
title: Mathematical Knowledge for Teaching (MKT) model with six domains of teacher content knowledge
description: The article frames teacher knowledge using Shulman's model and Ball and colleagues' MKT model, which "addresses how a teacher uses mathematics for teaching." Under subject matter knowledge sit common content knowledge, specialized content knowledge, and horizon content knowledge; under pedagogical content knowledge sit knowledge of content and students, of content and teaching, and of content and curriculum. The study's instrument (CKT-M Measures) derives from this research continuum, and the article argues preservice teachers need specialized content knowledge — mathematics for teaching — not just factual knowledge.
requirements: The model distinguishes knowledge unique to teaching from knowledge not unique to teaching, so use requires attending to that distinction
constraints: The article applies the model to elementary geometry content knowledge for preservice teachers in a methods course setting
target_learning_goals: specialized content knowledge of geometry for teaching
examples: The CKT-M Measures geometry section, developed by Learning Mathematics for Teaching at University of Michigan, was used to measure change in geometry content knowledge
key_sources: Fatma Aslan-Tutak and Thomasenia Lott Adams. (2015). A Study of Geometry Content Knowledge of Elementary Preservice Teachers. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 7(3), 301-318. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1068059

article_title: Using multilevel modeling to evaluate science literacy and technology course of the Indonesian non-science students
citation: Bayu Setiaji, Purwoko Haryanto Santoso, Khafidh Nur Aziz, Heri Retnawati, and Moh Khairudin. (2023). Using multilevel modeling to evaluate science literacy and technology course of the Indonesian non-science students. Identifier: none printed in text.
title: Science literacy and technology course (MKU 6217): compulsory science-literacy course for non-science undergraduates at UNY
description: MKU 6217 is a compulsory first-year course at Universitas Negeri Yogyakarta, offered since 2020 and "predominantly offered for non-science students to furnish their competencies in being the future Indonesian educators". Topics span nature of science, scientific method, civilization development, universe as a system, science-technology implementation, and big ideas in science. It was delivered via the Moodle-based BESMART LMS with distance learning during the pandemic transition, and evaluated here with the SLA-D, a midterm exam, and SLA-MB.
requirements: Delivered through the BESMART Moodle-based LMS for administering the course to all students
constraints: Findings may differ at other universities within the Indonesian education system; the study did not compare non-science with science majors
target_learners: Non-science first-year undergraduate students across departments and faculties
target_learning_goals: Science literacy including principles of scientific investigation and nature of science
examples: Evaluated in 2022/2023 with 160 students from marketing (n = 38), accounting (n = 39), Javanese language (n = 51), and dance education (n = 50) departments in two faculties
key_sources: Bayu Setiaji, Purwoko Haryanto Santoso, Khafidh Nur Aziz, Heri Retnawati, and Moh Khairudin. (2023). Using multilevel modeling to evaluate science literacy and technology course of the Indonesian non-science students. Identifier: none printed in text. https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06782
